annotations.text:
ITERATION 2 — three ways to judge on iPhone 15 Pro portrait, installed as a PWA.

The header, reciter chip and page selector are now recreated from Header.tsx and PageNav.tsx rather than invented. The page selector floats in the Mushaf's own centre marginalia slot, exactly as the app does it, which costs no height at all.

The status bar (59) and home indicator (34) are reserved but the background paints through them, as it will once index.html gets viewport-fit=cover.

Tap around: score and mistake sheets open, Undo removes the Faṣāḥa mark, Finish opens Review and save. Every frame has a dark switch; A also has tweaks for the colour treatment, the criterion count, what number the chips carry, and whether the last-mark strip appears at all.

A · STATUS DOCK — the lead

Page 377×554, the largest a 393pt phone allows at 8px margins. Dock 94, fixed.

The dock's top row morphs: normally one chip per criterion, and for a few seconds after a mark it becomes the last-action strip with Undo. Both are 44 high, so nothing on screen moves — it replaces the chips rather than popping over them.

The strip carries its own dismiss, and the lastMark tweak turns it off for good. Either way the mistake stays in the log, so nothing is lost by closing it.

Chips are stacked, so nothing is abbreviated — not Faṣāḥa, not Adu / Raagu — and the strip renders 1, 2, 3 or 4 cells. Try the criteria tweak.

Below about 312px of dock width the Score label and the strip's timestamp drop out rather than clip.

B · COLLAPSIBLE LEDGER

Same page size. Peek 76 high; expanded it rises over the lower page rather than resizing it.

Shown expanded — tap the header to collapse. Closest to the desktop rail, and the only one where all four criteria and the Adu / Raagu control are legible together.

Costs: the score is either a 28px number strip or a panel covering the Quran. There is no middle setting.

C · LIVE MODE / REVIEW MODE

Same page size. One 60-high bar, and no score at all while listening.

Quietest screen and the largest Undo target. "Review & finish" opens the same Review and save screen on page 2 — so C is the cheapest of the three to build, not the most expensive.

Still your call, not mine: should the running total be visible during recitation? That is a competition rule, not a layout choice.

WHERE ALL THREE END UP — App.tsx:307 → App.tsx:327

Finish recitation opens Review and save, which refuses to save until Adu / Raagu carries a mark; saving then hands over to the next reciter. Both screens are shared by A, B and C, so the only real difference between the three directions is what happens while the judge is listening.

Review and save is the existing FinishDialog composition — head, scrolling body, pinned actions — at phone width. It already behaves as a full-screen sheet at min(620px, 100vw − 32px). The safe-area padding drawn here is a proposal: .finish-dialog uses calc(100dvh − 32px) with no env() term today, so on a real iPhone it would sit under the Dynamic Island.

Flip the blocked tweak on Review to see the "Adu / Raagu not entered" state, drawn with the app's own error colours.

SHARED PARTS · 1:1

01 — The header at 55 (today) and 64 (proposed). Removing the page-selector band frees 44px, and the Mushaf cannot use it: at 8px margins the page is 377 wide, and 377 ÷ 0.68 = 554, so extra height does nothing. The header is where that space can go.

03 — A judge is assigned 1 to 4 criteria (one-each panels give exactly one; Faṣāḥa and Adu / Raagu are optional), so the strip is drawn at every count.

04 — The colour treatment as a setting: off, earned, always. Shown early in a recitation, when only one criterion has cost anything, which is where the three differ. Primary ink clears 14.4:1 on every wash; secondary text on a tinted chip must be --ink-2, since --ink-3 on the Jalī wash measures 4.43:1 and misses AA.

07 / 08 — Both Adu / Raagu input modes, since aduRaaguInputMode is a saved preference.

The Quran text is Surah al-Mulk from public/pages/p562.json, unchanged. The app sets it in a per-page QCF font whose glyphs fill each printed line exactly; that font could not be fetched here, so the words are re-packed to fit HafsUthmanic. Words, order and marks are real — only the line breaks differ from the print.
